source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: PDF page 20 'Recipients born during the period from January 1, 1946 through December 31, 1952' (a retirement subtraction or a Tier 2 Michigan Standard Deduction) and NOTE ('may only claim one'); PDF pages 22-23 questions 1-6 (complete Worksheet 2 and Worksheet 3.3 and claim the most beneficial); Worksheet 2 (PDF page 18); Worksheet 3.3 (PDF page 25); Schedule 1 lines 14, 25, 27; MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = private pension 45,000.00 + interest 15,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 85,500.00. Federal taxable income = 85,500.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 67,750.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (born 1950, past 67): two options, claim one. Worksheet 3.3: line 4 49,422.75 (49,423), line 5 45,000.00, line 6 45,000.00. Worksheet 2: line 7 Tier 2 = 20,000.00. Retirement subtraction: line 14 = 85,500.00 - SS 25,500.00 - 45,000.00 = 15,000.00; less exemption 5,800.00 = 9,200.00; tax 391.00. Tier 2 instead: 85,500.00 - 25,500.00 - 20,000.00 - 5,800.00 = 34,200.00, tax 1,453.50. The retirement subtraction is more beneficial, so Form 4884 line 19 45,000.00 goes on Schedule 1 line 27 and line 25 is left blank. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 9,200.00 x 0.0425 = 391.00. No credits; state income tax 391.00.
